Behavioral Health Scenario 11 – Emergency Department Suicide Identification, Assessment, Safety, and Follow-Up
Scenario 11.1 – Patient Narrative
Maria, a 28-year-old with chronic pain and recent job loss, presents to a general medical emergency department (ED) for severe insomnia and anxiety. During triage, the nurse administers an ED-appropriate suicide risk screener (e.g., C-SSRS ED Screener with Triage Points or ASQ). Maria endorses suicidal ideation and reports a recent self-harm behavior.

The EHR captures screener responses as discrete structured data, derives an outcome (negative / non-acute positive / acute positive) using configurable rules, and then:
• Communicates status to the whole ED team via a visible ED trackboard / chart banner indicator, and
• Separately routes time-sensitive protocol work via role-based Tasks and a clinician-facing advisory that provides one-click access to the appropriate order set/checklists.

For positive screens, the EHR supports rapid mitigation (environment/room clearance checklist, belongings documentation, and observation/1:1 sitter workflow with appropriate provider authorization), followed by brief assessment and/or full suicide risk assessment (e.g., Brief Suicide Safety Assessment when ASQ is used; SAFE-T with C-SSRS when indicated).

Following assessment, the care team determines Maria can be discharged with collaborative safety planning, lethal means counseling, and rapid follow-up. At discharge, the EHR automatically includes (and prints or portal-delivers) a patient-facing safety plan and suicide-specific discharge instructions with crisis resources, and transmits a transition-of-care packet to outpatient providers while initiating post-discharge caring contacts/follow-up calls.

Scenario 11.2 – Screening and Identification
In the ED, suicide risk screening is performed early (often at triage) using a validated tool appropriate to age and setting. The EHR supports fast capture of structured screening results, applies rules to identify positive/acute screens, and (a) communicates screening status via visible indicators and (b) routes the next required steps as time-sensitive tasks/advisories without relying on clinician memory.

Scenario 11.3 – Immediate Safety / Mitigation
For acute positive or otherwise high-risk presentations, the ED must rapidly mitigate environmental and procedural risks. The EHR supports a standardized mitigation checklist/order set, documents observation level and environmental safety actions, and ensures provider authorization/countersignature where required.

Scenario 11.4 – Brief Assessment and Suicide Risk Assessment
After a positive screen, a trained clinician completes a brief suicide safety assessment (especially when ASQ is used and the screen is non-acute positive) to determine next steps. When indicated, the care team completes a structured suicide risk assessment (e.g., SAFE-T with C-SSRS). The EHR captures key assessment elements as discrete data and supports disposition decision-making.

Scenario 11.5 – Boarding and Reassessment

Scenario 11.6 – Safety Planning and Discharge Planning
Before ED discharge of a patient with suicide risk, best practice is to create or update a collaborative safety plan, provide lethal means counseling (a distinct intervention), and arrange rapid follow-up. The EHR supports structured, versioned safety plans; structured lethal means safety actions; and discharge-step completion with automatic inclusion/printing of required patient materials.

Scenario 11.7 – Care Transitions and Follow-Up
The EHR supports closed-loop care transitions from the ED by transmitting key suicide-related information (as permitted) to next providers, arranging rapid follow-up, and initiating post-discharge contacts (caring contacts and phone follow-up) with monitoring and escalation.
